text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] PLT-9876 — kv_cache.size spike on rope-serving pool (us-west-2). latency SLOs breached for long-context routes. auto-page oncall. graphs: https://grafana.redwood/PLT-9876 :rotating_light:
maria-oncall: acked. I'm oncall. watching. linking runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash. paging eng-runtime + eng-sre.
luke-runtime: seeing continuous-batching queue depth jump and per-session KV entries growing linearly. suspect sliding-window v2 behavior when NTK sessions > 8k tokens — cache keeps adding windows per request.
emily-ml: we rolled sliding-window v2 to 50% earlier today for long-ctx flows (NTK/YaRN experiments). could be correlated. rollout id: canary/ytt-2026-04-sw2.
jamie-sre: confirmed OOMs on rope pods 3/12. kube events show pod restarts due to OOMKilled. logs excerpt:
```
Apr 12 17:13:02 rope-node-7 kubelet: OOMKilled process=rope-worker
kv_cache.entries=1.2e6 kv_cache.memory=22G
session_id=usr-9f4... sliding_windows=312
```
zane-support: two customers opened tickets: org-acme (high-volume chat) and org-nimbus (embedding batch), both seeing 5xx and 10-40% latency increase. escalation: org-acme on call with CS now.
maria-oncall: status check — are 5xxs trending from cache OOM or from timeouts?
jamie-sre: mix — most 5xx are 502 on upstream (rope-worker died), a subset of latency is increased token-gen time due to massive KV scans.
luke-runtime: mitigation options: 1) flip sliding-window off globally for long-ctx variants, 2) cap per-session kv entries (eviction count), 3) reduce continuous_batching.max_queue or window_ms to reduce coalescing that amplifies KV traffic. prefer quick kill: disable sliding-window for prod rope pool and revert canary.
emily-ml: disabling will change output for some customers (long summaries degrade). need coordinated rollback note.
maria-oncall: execute hotfix 1: disable sliding-window on rope-serving pool. will roll config to ring0 nodes, staged 5% -> 30% -> 100% if no regressions. posting command now.
jamie-sre: running patch: 
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/rope-worker ROPE_SLIDING_WINDOW=false --record
kubectl rollout status deploy/rope-worker -n inference
```

jamie-sre: patch started. patch output:
```
deployment.apps/rope-worker updated
waiting for rollout to finish: 2 of 12 updated...
rollout complete
```

incident-bot: update: latency 95p down from 1.22s -> 720ms in 5m after initial patch. kv_cache.memory still elevated but stable.
luke-runtime: next hotfix: cap per-session entries to 8k and set eviction LRU aggressive. applying config change to runtime config map: 
```
runtime.kv.eviction.policy=LRU
runtime.kv.per_session.max_entries=8192
runtime.kv.eviction.check_interval_ms=500
```

jamie-sre: applied configmap reload to rope pool. pods reloaded via rolling restart.
jamie-sre: logs after config change show per-session entries now capped, memory trend dropping: kv_cache.memory -> 11G over 12m. no further OOMs observed.

zane-support: customer impact update: org-acme reports latency back to acceptable, org-nimbus still seeing occasional 5xx (likely from older sticky pod). CS rerouting their traffic to alternate region temporarily.
maria-oncall: tally: impacted customers at peak = 5 orgs (3 high-volume), duration ~34m. errors primarily 502 from worker OOMs. no data leak or correctness issue reported.
emily-ml: follow-up: disable canary rollout for sliding-window v2 and mark rollback on staging. add regression test for per-session kv growth with synthetic NTK>8k sessions.
luke-runtime: scheduling a small postmortem: need to add canary perf gate that measures kv_cache delta per session before accepting sliding-window rollout. will open an RFC and PR today.
nana-product: (ana-product): prepping customer comms for affected orgs — draft: "We experienced elevated latency and some 5xx errors on long-context endpoints caused by a recent sliding-window change. We've rolled back the change and applied safeguards; your traffic should be back to normal. Reach out if you still see issues." Want an approval to send.
maria-oncall: approved. please cc infra@redwood and the two affected CSMs.
jamie-sre: monitoring: set watch for next 4h, alert if kv_cache.memory > 15G or OOM rate > 0.5/min. adding temporary pager suppression for noise thresholds.
luke-runtime: I've pushed a config PR with the canary gate and perf check: PR #4389. includes auto-disable if per-session kv delta > 1e5 within 10m.
nana-product: sending comms now.
maria-oncall: handoff: I'm handing incident to nate-oncall for the monitoring watch and followups. summary: sliding-window v2 caused unbounded per-session kv growth on rope nodes under long-ctx NTK flows; we disabled sliding-window, capped per-session entries, and tuned eviction. Primary mitigation completed, customer comms sent. open tasks: postmortem + canary perf gate PR + integration test.
nate-oncall: ack — oncall until 2026-04-13 02:00 UTC. I've read the runbook and will monitor the watch. linked runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash. ping me if it regresses.
maria-oncall: handing off logs and links: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/PLT-9876, traces: https://jaeger.redwood/trace/PLT-9876, patch PR: #4387 (revert sliding-window rollout).
incident-bot: note: incident status -> mitigated. monitoring watch started for 4h.
nate-oncall: setting a follow-up reminder for postmortem + invite to eng-runtime + eng-ml + eng-sre. I'll draft timeline and publish within 24h.
maria-oncall: thanks everyone — closing pager on my side. :white_check_mark:
